answer.reason: Based on prior knowledge of Idaho's labor market, the proposed correction to B is not supported. Idaho's total nonfarm employment was roughly 820,000-830,000 in late 2024, and construction (NAICS 23) accounted for roughly 8-9% of jobs (~70,000-75,000) after years of rapid construction growth in the Boise area. QCEW covered employment is not seasonally adjusted, and December is a seasonal trough, so a December 2024 construction level near 68,000-69,000 is consistent with these benchmarks. A figure of 52,471 would put construction at only ~6% of state employment, a level Idaho last had around 2020-2021, not 2024. Since no verbatim source text was supplied (only a URL), I cannot quote the CSV directly, but the plausibility balance strongly favors A; the user's correction to B appears to reflect a data-pulling error (52,471 is consistent with other states' December 2024 construction levels, such as Arkansas).
